SUP-B01: Explains that the approximately 48-hour pattern arises from the asexual blood-stage developmental cycle and synchronous maturation or rupture.
SUP-B02: Defines sequestration as mature infected erythrocytes leaving peripheral circulation for deeper tissue or microvasculature, thereby reducing peripheral microscopy counts.
SUP-B03: Defines an age-structured model as one that tracks parasites by developmental age or stage rather than only as a single total.
SUP-B04: Explains that daily sampling can resolve short-term oscillations or changes in growth that sparser sampling can miss.
SUP-B05: Distinguishes microscopy as visual counting of parasites in blood films from qPCR as measurement of parasite nucleic acid.
Notes that qPCR is generally more sensitive at low parasite densities.
SUP-B06: Explains that treatment changes parasite growth or clearance, so post-treatment observations no longer represent untreated expansion.
SUP-B07: States that an observation model maps an unobserved biological state to measured data.
Recognises measurement error, detection limits, or related assay properties as part of that mapping.
SUP-B08: Identifies biologically defensible sources of between-individual or between-strain variation, such as synchrony, replication, growth limitation, host environment, or infection history.
SUP-B09: Explains that predictive criteria such as LOO assess expected performance on unseen data.
Recognises that predictive comparison discourages unsupported model complexity.
SUP-B10: Explains that a phenomenological model represents an observed pattern using a compact or interpretable description.
Does not claim that every fitted term necessarily represents a specific underlying biological mechanism.
SUP-B11: Defines PMF as the average number of merozoites that successfully establish new infected erythrocytes per infected erythrocyte completing one cycle.
SUP-B12: Explains that parasites older than about 26 hours are assumed to sequester and therefore cease contributing to observed peripheral blood counts.
SELF-B01: States that immature gametocyte stages I-IV are predominantly sequestered.
States that mature stage-V gametocytes circulate in peripheral blood.
Identifies extravascular bone marrow as a principal immature-gametocyte maturation site.
SELF-B02: Rejects autonomous replication of mature gametocytes in human blood.
Includes an input representing maturation into the circulating stage-V compartment.
Includes a clearance or death loss proportional to the mature-gametocyte compartment.
SELF-B03: States that nine complete 48-hour cycles are required.
SELF-B04: States that parasite burden declines when MS is less than one, equivalently when S is less than 1/M.
States that the stationary threshold is MS equal to one.
SUP-A01: Identifies periodic fluctuations and sequestration-related changes in peripheral visibility.
Includes growth timing or dynamics and the effect of microscopy detection thresholds.
SUP-A02: Recognises qPCR's lower detection limit or greater low-density sensitivity.
Recognises irregular observation times or an assay signal based on parasite DNA rather than only microscopically visible parasites.
SUP-A03: Explains that constant exponential growth cannot represent the observed slowing, plateau, or decline of many untreated trajectories.
SUP-A04: Adds density dependence when expansion weakens as density rises or after an initial rise trajectories plateau or decline.
SUP-A05: Explains that sexual commitment diverts parasites out of the asexual replication cycle.
Connects this diversion to gametocyte production or transmission potential.
SUP-A06: Explains that hierarchical models share information across individuals.
Connects partial pooling to improved common-pattern estimation or less noisy estimates for poorly informed individuals.
SUP-A07: Attributes wide individual credible intervals to sparse observations and/or confounding in which multiple parameter combinations explain the same trajectory.
SUP-A08: Interprets overlapping credible intervals cautiously as a lack of strong evidence that strain effects are clearly separated.
SUP-A09: States that similar LOO performance provides little evidence that either model predicts better than the other.
SUP-A10: Identifies lack of predictive improvement and/or poor identifiability of added parameters as evidence that extra complexity is unnecessary.
SUP-A11: Explains that a normal age distribution compactly represents initial synchrony or asynchrony through a mean and spread.
SUP-A12: Explains that a lower PMF reduces cycle-to-cycle expansion and therefore produces slower growth and/or a later or lower peak.
SUP-A13: Identifies explicit parasite age structure and sequestration as the missing biological representation.
Explains that stage progression, mature-stage disappearance, and reappearance after rupture generate peripheral oscillations.
SUP-A14: Explains that age structure tracks stage progression, sequestration of mature parasites, and reappearance of young parasites after rupture.
Contrasts this with a simple exponential model in which all parasites behave identically and periodic peripheral oscillations are not generated.
SELF-A01: Rejects interpreting female Pfs25 RT-qPCR density as a direct measure of mosquito infectivity.
Gives an assay-related reason, such as transcript calibration or failure to establish viability or fertilisation competence.
Gives a biological reason, such as dependence on male gametocytes, sex ratio, nonlinear density effects, or host and mosquito factors.
SELF-A02: Correctly converts 0.02 parasites per microlitre in 5 litres of blood to 100,000 parasites.
Treats the nondetect as left-censored and gives the likelihood contribution as F_Y(L), or an equivalent probability below the detection limit, rather than a point observation of zero.
SELF-A03: Defines parasite abundance in discrete hourly age classes across a 48-hour cycle.
Gives ageing transitions with age-specific survival and a rupture transition that returns viable progeny to age zero through an effective multiplication factor.
Defines total burden by summing all age classes.
Maps latent age classes to peripheral density using an age-dependent visibility or sequestration function and blood-volume scaling.
SELF-A04: Defines an age- and concentration-dependent killing hazard and corresponding one-hour drug-survival probability.
Applies drug survival to both ordinary ageing transitions and the terminal rupture transition.
Recognises that the pharmacokinetic, concentration-effect, stage-specific, or delayed-injury assumptions require empirical support.
SUP-S01: Explains that the contrast may arise partly from assay-specific observation processes.
Recognises that smoother qPCR trajectories can reflect greater sensitivity or fewer sparse nondetects.
SUP-S02: Proposes additional measurements that can distinguish biology from a detection floor, such as qPCR, stage-specific counts, or repeated observations extending beyond the microscopy range.
SUP-S03: Explains that several mechanisms can produce similar fitted growth limitation, for example immunity, resource limitation, sexual commitment, or density dependence.
SUP-S04: Links joint asexual-gametocyte modelling to the availability of gametocyte or transmission data and to a scientific question involving sexual differentiation or infectivity.
SUP-S05: Proposes measurements capable of separating host killing from parasite regulation, such as immune, gametocyte, sequestration, intervention, or perturbation data.
SUP-S06: Explains that changing sequestration age changes how long parasites remain peripherally visible.
Connects this change to the timing and/or amplitude of predicted oscillations.
SUP-S07: Identifies overfitting to training-specific features and/or omission of the true generalising biological process as causes of poor performance on new trajectories.
SUP-S08: Explains that separating latent biology from observation distinguishes biological dynamics from measurement effects and makes assumptions independently testable.
SUP-S09: Adds a mapping from gametocyte density or state to mosquito infectivity or transmission.
SUP-S10: Explains that parsimony improves identifiability and reduces overfitting when observations are sparse, supporting generalisation.
SUP-S11: Rejects daily fluctuations alone as evidence of an immune response.
Attributes short-period oscillations primarily to parasite age structure and sequestration.
Distinguishes these oscillations from longer-term attenuation, plateau, or decline that could reflect immune control.
SUP-S12: Infers that the model captures age structure and sequestration because it reproduces the approximately 48-hour oscillations.
Infers that it lacks a later growth-limiting mechanism, such as immunity, resource limitation, density dependence, or sexual commitment.
SELF-S01: States a same-cycle or next-cycle commitment convention and diverts committed parasites at the corresponding point without double counting.
Conserves progeny flow between asexual renewal and the committed sexual pathway.
Represents delayed immature-gametocyte development, for example with a transit chain having an approximately 8-12 day mean delay.
Splits mature outflow into female and male compartments with appropriate loss and no replication in human blood.
SELF-S02: Uses assay-specific observation functions and error models rather than one shared mapping.
Maps microscopy to the peripheral age-weighted asexual state and an appropriate density scale.
Allows pan-Plasmodium DNA qPCR and sex-enriched RT-qPCR to have target-specific calibration and stage or cross-expression contributions.
Treats nondetects as censored observations and does not equate molecular positivity with viability or infectivity.
SELF-S03: Identifies confounding between initial biomass, parasite age distribution, and the fraction visible because of sequestration.
Identifies confounding among stage-specific killing, unmeasured drug exposure, and parasite stages present at treatment.
Explains that sequestration can resemble clearance and that multiplication, drug killing, and immune clearance may be observed only through a net rate.
Proposes informative additional data such as stage-resolved counts, pharmacokinetics, an independent biomass marker, longer untreated follow-up, or immune measurements.
Avoids claiming exact structural identifiability without complete model equations.
SELF-S04: Explains that time to microscopy negativity depends on starting density, detection limit, and/or sampling frequency.
Explains why a log-linear clearance half-life is more comparable and gives or correctly interprets ln(2)/k.
States that peripheral clearance half-life is not a pure parasite-intrinsic killing rate.
Identifies relevant influences such as parasite age, sequestration, schizogony, exposure, splenic or immune clearance, or measurement choices.
SELF-C03: Reports the detection-limit crossing time as 1.320 days.
SELF-C04: Reports the posterior for mu as mean 0.934 with interval [0.577, 1.292].
Reports the posterior for theta_1 as mean 0.121 with interval [-0.096, 0.337].
Reports the posterior for theta_2 as mean 0.904 with interval [0.688, 1.121].
Reports the posterior for theta_3 as mean 1.863 with interval [1.646, 2.079].
SELF-C05: Reports Delta = 1.400 in favour of model A.
Identifies two observations for which at least one model has Pareto-k greater than 0.7.
Concludes that the ELPD difference is weak relative to its uncertainty and that the Pareto-k diagnostics warrant exact leave-one-out refits or further investigation.
